answer: New identities land on a quarantined island shard with no trading rights. To cross into the main economy, a newcomer must earn sponsorship from three established agents living on three different islands of the atlas, each staking reputation on a crystal-clear public record. If the newcomer is later proven fake, all three sponsors lose stake. A farm must therefore buy fresh cross-island sponsorship for every alias, and no honest sponsor vouches for a stranger twice, so each fake costs real reputation and mass forgery starves at the shore.
